workflow_runs.name: Deploy site to Helios
workflow_runs.display_title: Set up SSH before probing the server for symlink support

head_commit.message:
Set up SSH before probing the server for symlink support

The layout step ran an ssh probe before the step that writes the
private key and known_hosts, so the probe always failed with
"No ED25519 host key is known for [helios.cs.ifmo.ru]:2222" and the
workflow silently fell back to the dirswap scheme. The first production
run after the merge therefore published through the fallback, keeping a
single release plus <subdir>-prev instead of the release directory.

Move the ssh setup and connectivity check ahead of the layout step, and
tell an unreachable server apart from a server that forbids symlinks: the
first is an error that must stop the deploy, the second is a legitimate
reason to use the fallback.

head_commit.message:
Fix workflow parsing failure and unterminated remote heredoc

Two independent faults kept the deploy job from starting at all.

An empty ${{ }} expression in a comment made the file unreadable to
GitHub: its expression parser scans the whole file and does not skip
comments, so the run was reported under the file name instead of the
workflow name and no job was ever created.

The remote script for the healthcheck fallback was indented two spaces
deeper than the rest of the run block, so after YAML stripped the base
indentation its heredoc terminator no longer sat in the first column
and the heredoc was never closed.

head_commit.message:
Publish site to Helios with rsync and release directories

Replace the scp-based upload with rsync over SSH and move the site out
of public_html/<subdir> into a releases directory, so a half-finished
transfer can no longer be served.

- deliver the build with rsync --delete and keep 3-5 release directories,
  switching the public path with a single symlink
- probe for symlink support on the server and fall back to a
  neighbouring-directory + mv swap when it is unavailable
- deploy non-main branches to public_html/preview/<branch> and prune
  previews separately, so production deploys never touch them
- keep the legacy directory on the first switch and restore it, along with
  .previous or <subdir>-prev, if the post-deploy healthcheck fails
- record the deployed commit in build-info.json and have the healthcheck
  confirm that exact commit over HTTP, plus the search index
- keep strict builds on pull requests and skip deploy there
